title: UFO panic in the skies over Mexico! The truth came out later
excerpt: A bright cone-shaped object gliding in the sky over Mexico left citizens astonished. It turned out that the images thought to be a UFO were caused by light reflection formed during SpaceX's Starship rocket test flight.
content:
22.11.2026 10:00

A bright cone-shaped object gliding in the sky over Mexico left citizens astonished. It turned out that the images thought to be a UFO were caused by light reflection formed during SpaceX's Starship rocket test flight.

The cone-shaped bright object gliding in the sky over Mexico drew the attention of nearby citizens. Many people grabbed their mobile phones and recorded the images, while comments were made on social media that the object could be a UFO. However, investigations into the images revealed a different explanation that attracted attention: the bright formation is assessed to be connected to SpaceX's Starship rocket test flight.

IT WAS THOUGHT TO BE A UFO

The bright formation seen in different parts of Mexico on the evening of Friday, November 13, was recorded especially in the states of Mexico City, Puebla, and Chiapas. Images of the lights slowly moving across the sky and resembling a cone or fan shape spread quickly. While some citizens thought it was an unidentified flying object (UFO), those who recorded the images drew attention to the object's size and movement.

THE CAUSE OF THE MYSTERIOUS IMAGE BECAME KNOWN

In the examinations carried out, it was determined that the lights in the images were connected to the 15th test flight of the Starship spacecraft developed by SpaceX. The vehicle, launched from the Starbase facility in Texas, could be seen from different parts of Mexico during the flight.

The optical phenomenon, which experts call the "jellyfish effect," is formed by gases left by the rocket at high altitude reflecting sunlight. Even if it is dark on the ground, gases at high altitude continue to receive sunlight. This creates a bright image in the sky resembling a cone, fan, or jellyfish.

STARSHIP CARRIED 26 SATELLITES INTO ORBIT

In Starship's 15th test flight, the goal was to place 26 Starlink V3 satellites into orbit. While the spacecraft reached orbit and carried out satellite deployment, the return and catch phase of the rocket booster named Super Heavy could not be completed as planned. The booster was destroyed over the Gulf of Mexico. Starship, after completing 14 laps around the Earth, returned to its facility in Texas.
